subject: Post-call recap: Horizon Health — SLO & budget trade-offs / next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: SLOs, projected volumes, and pricing guardrails

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached a one-page MAP (mutual action plan) for the POC.

Call highlights:
- Target product: clinical triage chat embedded in Horizon’s provider portal (primary users: nurses + triage staff).
- Estimated ramp: month 1 = ~50M tokens, month 3 = ~120M tokens, Q4 steady-state = ~200M tokens/month. These are rough; please correct if off.
- Primary success metrics: response latency < 500ms perceived for chat responses (streaming preferred), model quality pass rate on 10k eval prompts > 92%.
- Budget range discussed: ~$5k–$15k/month initially. You mentioned a target unit economics goal — approx $/1M tokens you’d like to hit?

Trade-offs we called out:
- Streaming vs batched generation: streaming improves perceived latency (first-token-to-client) but can increase per-token unit cost slightly depending on model/wire overhead.
- Dedicated reserved capacity reduces $/1M tokens compared to hosted burst but requires a committed spend.
- Aggressive quantization (e.g., 4-bit) and model distillation reduce cost but can impact subtlety on clinical phrasing — we’ll validate on your eval set.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You confirm expected monthly token cadence and a target $/1M tokens number (ballpark is fine).
2) We do a 3-week POC: mixed mode (streaming for UI + small batching for backfill) to measure real latency and token counts.
3) Redwood provides two pricing scenarios and a short procurement checklist (SOC2 evidence, PO template, sample SOW).

Attachments: Horizon_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP + milestones).

If that looks right I’ll draft the POC scope and pricing options (hosted trial vs. dedicated reserved) and loop in procurement.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Nguyen <alice@horizonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2027-02-11T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLOs, projected volumes, and pricing guardrails

Ben — thanks for the recap and MAP. Couple quick points / clarifications:

- Volume: those ramps are in the right direction. For procurement, please assume: month 1 = 50M, month 2 = 90M, month 3 = 150M, steady = 200M. We’ll aim to finalize with a 6-month review.
- Budget / unit economics: long-term procurement target we’d prefer to be around $600–$900 per 1M tokens. For the pilot we can accept a higher introductory rate if there’s a clear path to the target with commit.
- Latency: chat UI is sensitive to first-byte. If streaming gives perceived latency under 300ms for small responses (~64 tokens) that’s ideal. We can tolerate p95 up to 800ms for longer writes but tail behavior matters.

Questions:
1) Can you outline approximate $/1M for hosted vs dedicated vs dedicated+quant? Please give both list and committed (discounted) rates so procurement can see options.
2) Does Redwood support automatic fallback to a smaller model when capacity spikes to keep UI online?
3) What evidence do you have around KV/cache hit rates reducing token counts for dialog-style workloads?

Procurement is CC'd and will take the MAP and PO template.

— Alice
Alice Nguyen | Dir. Product, Digital Experience | Horizon Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: pricing sketches + recommended config for Horizon POC

Internal notes for POC pricing deck. These are conservative estimates based on recent similar customers (chat UI, mixed throughput):

Unit economics (approx $ per 1M tokens):
- Hosted (no commit, streaming optimized): list = $1,050 / 1M tokens. Expected p50 latency good, p95 varies by region.
- Dedicated small pool (reserved monthly, moderate commit): list = $580 / 1M tokens; committed effective = $420 / 1M tokens with 6-month commit and modest CU (compute unit) guarantee.
- Dedicated medium + 4-bit quant (reserved + quant tuning): list = $360 / 1M tokens; committed effective = $320 / 1M tokens for Q4 steady-state volumes (200M+/mo) — assumes some minor quality drop we’ll validate.

Latency trade-offs and configuration notes:
- Streaming (chunked token streaming) yields best perceived latency for chat; it slightly increases per-token request overhead (small network frames) but saves user wait time. Good fit for short-turn interactions.
- Small batching (continuous batching with tight window) reduces per-token CPU cost and is best for backfill or non-interactive calls. It adds scheduling wait ~20–60ms average depending on traffic.
- KV/prefix cache: for dialog flows with high repetition (patient context + templated prompts) we often see 10%–30% token savings on first pass, rising to 40%–60% on repeat flows once cache warms. We'll instrument metrics in the POC.

Fallbacks & reliability:
- Automatic fallback to a smaller model variant is supported by policy routing. We can set a policy to fallback to a lower-cost model (e.g., med -> small) when p95 queueing exceeds a threshold or when capacity signals high utilization. Quality regression alerting will be in the console.

Recommended POC config (to measure latency and token economics):
- 3 weeks, mixed-mode: streaming for UI, small batching for scheduled workflows.
- Run dedicated-small for business hours (M–F, 7AM–7PM PST) with hosted-pro fallback for off-hours.
- Instrument token-level cost, p50/p95/p99 latency (first-byte and full-response), and cache hit rate.

Suggested pricing offer for procurement (pilot special):
- Pilot: $750 / 1M tokens for first 3 months (hosted + reserved blended), credit cap of $25k.
- If Horizon commits to 6-month reserved capacity (est. 150M/mo commit), effective rate targets: $420–$320 / 1M depending on quantization acceptance and reserved tier.

I’ll pull this into a short slide and include a two-column hosted vs dedicated pricing table. Ben — can you push the MAP and PO to Alice/procurement and ask for any legal or SOC2 evidence they need?

— Marissa

From: Alice Nguyen <alice@horizonhealth.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@horizonhealth.com
Date: 2027-02-13T14:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLOs, projected volumes, and pricing guardrails

Thanks Marissa — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups:

- Tail concerns: our compliance team is demanding a p99 policy for peak windows; can we show historical p99 numbers for a comparable customer and also include an SLO document that spells out fallbacks/SLI definitions?
- Streaming + fallback: sounds good. How large is the quality delta you typically see when falling back to a smaller model? We can tolerate small factuality differences but not hallucinations for clinical phrasing.
- Caching: great to hear on numbers. Can you include an example metric line (e.g., token reduction pre/post caching) in the MAP so procurement can reason about billing variance?

Procurement: we’d like the PO template and the SOC2 summary. Procurement, what internal PO cadence do you need to approve a pilot?

— Alice

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@horizonhealth.com>, procurement@horizonhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLOs, projected volumes, and pricing guardrails — next steps & offer

Alice / Procurement — summary and immediate next steps. I’m attaching the MAP, PO template, and a short SOC2 extract for now (attached in repo).

Quick answers:
- p99 behavior: we can provide historical p99s from a comparable health-care customer in the same dedicated-small tier under similar ingress. I’ll pull anonymized numbers and include them in the SLO appendix.
- Quality delta on fallback: typical med->small fallback yields a drop in subjective quality ~5–10% on sensitive prompts in our internal eval sets; factual hallucination increase is small but not zero. Plan: enable fallback + automatic regression alerts and a hard circuit-breaker to suspend fallback if evals drift beyond threshold.
- Caching example: baseline prompt tokens 180 per session -> after prefix/KV caching average tokens per session dropped to 120 (33% reduction) in week 2 of cache warm-up during a pilot. I’ll include a chart in the MAP appendix.

Pilot offer (formalized):
- Duration: 3 weeks (PO to enable reserve and instrumentation).
- Pilot pricing: blended $750 / 1M tokens for first 90 days (applied as credit). Cap $25k in billable charges during pilot; any overage billed at list hosted rate.
- Committed option: 6-month reserved commit at estimated 150M/mo -> effective $420 / 1M; add-on quantized tier for 200M+/mo -> $320 / 1M contingent on quality acceptance.

Immediate asks from Horizon:
1) Procurement: return signed PO template for the pilot and list required legal contact + invoicing details.
2) Alice: confirm final target $/1M threshold you want Redwood to hold us to for the committed option (Marissa used $420–$320 target).
3) Engineering: provide the small eval set (anonymized) and a sample dialog flow to validate quantization and fallback behavior.

I’ll also schedule a 30-minute technical sync Monday to walk through fallback policy and instrumentation (invite to follow).

Attachments: Horizon_MAP_v1.pdf, PO_template_Horizon.xlsx, SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf (attachment stubs).

Thanks — Ben
